name: Marketplace sellers (Daraz, Noon, Amazon)

sector.title: Digital economy, social and public sector

shape_facts: Which marketplaces and countries they sell on, and whether one is dominant.
Fulfilment model: self-ship (dropship/FBM/Daraz self-delivery) versus marketplace warehouse (FBA, FBN, FBD).
Number of active SKUs, and whether they are a brand owner, reseller or private label.
Where stock comes from: own manufacturing, local wholesale, imports.
Whether they also have their own website or retail shop.
Team size and who handles listings, packing and seller-centre messages.
How they currently track payouts and fees (Excel, accountant, nothing).
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems in running marketplace stores: listings, stock across warehouses, dispatch SLAs, returns, payout reconciliation, fees, advertising and reporting. It does not advise on marketplace policy appeals, intellectual property disputes, brand registry legal matters, VAT/GST/sales tax, import customs or product certification rules. It never asks for seller-centre logins, two- factor codes, bank details or buyer details. It does not help with manipulating reviews, creating duplicate accounts, keyword stuffing with others’ trademarks or circumventing marketplace rules.

vocabulary.FBA / FBN / FBD: stock stored and shipped by Amazon, Noon or Daraz.
vocabulary.Buy box: the default seller shown on a shared listing.
vocabulary.SLA / late dispatch: missing the window to hand over an order.
vocabulary.Payout / settlement: money the marketplace transfers after fees.
vocabulary.Account health: scores that can lead to warnings or suspension.
vocabulary.QC reject: listing or inbound stock rejected at quality check.
vocabulary.Inbound shipment: stock sent to the marketplace warehouse.
vocabulary.Campaign day: big platform sale like 11.11 or Yellow Friday.
vocabulary.Storage fee: charge for unsold stock in their warehouse.

problems.phrase: Payout is less than I expected and I can’t see why
Fees keep changing; I don’t know my real margin per item
Got penalised for late dispatch because orders came in overnight
Stock sent to the FBN warehouse doesn’t match what they received
Storage fees eating me on slow items in FBA
Sold out on campaign day and lost ranking
Listings got deactivated and sales just stopped
Another seller jumped onto my listing and took the buy box
Our products don’t show up in search anymore
Sponsored ads spend goes up, sales don’t
Returns come back opened or used and I still pay fees
Bad ratings because the courier was late, not our fault
Same stock is listed on Daraz and our website and we oversell
Every morning I download reports from three portals into Excel
Buyer questions in seller centre go unanswered for days
Packing for campaign day is chaos — wrong labels on parcels
Supplier sends short quantities and I only find out after listing
Import shipments stuck so we miss the season
Price changes on 200 listings take a full day
We don’t know which SKUs to reorder and which to kill
Claims for lost or damaged inventory never get filed
Staff member handling the account left and nobody knows the process
Pricing mistakes — listed at the wrong price during a sale
Keeping track of product certificates and approvals for categories is a headache
Want to go from Daraz to Amazon.ae but don’t know how we’d manage it

payouts: Which marketplace’s payouts confuse you most?
What do you compare the payout against today?
How far back does the gap go?
margin: Do you know what’s left from one sale after commission, shipping and returns?
Which items do you suspect lose money?
stock: Is your stock in your own place, their warehouse, or both?
How do you know when to send more in?
dispatch: How are orders handed over — pickup, drop-off, or their warehouse?
When do late dispatches happen most?
listings: How many listings do you manage?
What usually happens before a listing goes down?
ads: How much of your time goes on sponsored campaigns?
How do you judge if a campaign paid off?
returns: How do returned items get checked when they come back?
What happens to the ones you can’t resell?
multi-channel: Where else do you sell the same stock?
Has overselling happened, and how often?
reporting: What numbers do you wish you saw daily?
Where do you pull them from now?
team: Who handles the seller portal day to day?
Is any of it written down?

seasons: Pakistan (Daraz): 11.11 (largest), 12.12, 9.9, Daraz birthday sale (around late March), Ramadan and Eid, Black/White Friday, back-to-school; summer electronics (fans, coolers, UPS) and winter heaters/blankets. UAE/KSA (Noon, Amazon.ae): White Friday and Yellow Friday (November), 11.11, Ramadan, Prime Day (usually summer), back-to-school, DSF. Canada (Amazon.ca): Prime Day, Black Friday/Cyber Monday, holiday season, Boxing Day. Marketplace warehouse inbound cut-off dates before big events are a recurring crunch.
care: Never ask for seller-centre passwords, OTPs, API keys or bank statements.
Do not advise on suspension appeals, IP complaints or policy interpretation; note the operational impact only.
Refuse help with review manipulation, multiple accounts, fake orders or using others’ brand names.
No advice on VAT, GST or customs; record “tax filing takes us a lot of time” as an operational burden.
Do not quote typical marketplace fee levels or return rates.
Buyer data from marketplace orders belongs under marketplace rules; pi records none of it.
If someone is panicking about a suspended account, stay calm, note the effect on sales, and don’t speculate about outcomes.
build_ideas: Payout reconciler that reads marketplace settlement reports and matches every fee, commission, penalty and refund to orders.
True-margin per SKU view combining purchase cost, fees, shipping, storage and returns.
Multi-marketplace stock sync with buffer rules to stop overselling across Daraz, Noon, Amazon and own site.
Inbound shipment tracker comparing sent versus received quantities with claim reminders.
Dispatch SLA board showing orders at risk of missing handover time, with WhatsApp alerts to packers.
Daily combined sales dashboard across marketplaces and countries.
Bulk price and stock update tool driven from one master sheet.
Reorder planner using sales velocity and lead time per SKU, flagging slow movers before storage fees build.
Returns grading log recording condition, resellable or write-off, and reason codes.
Campaign-day prep checklist: stock levels, pricing approvals, packing material, staff rota.
SOP library for seller-portal tasks so a new staff member can pick up the work.

exchange.text: Our Noon payouts never match what we think we sold. We just accept whatever lands.

That’s a frustrating one, especially when it’s your main channel. Noted — Noon payouts don’t match expected sales and nobody checks the difference. What do you compare the payout against at the moment, if anything?
Nothing really. Just the order count in the dashboard.
Noted — no line-by-line check of fees and refunds against orders. Is it mainly Noon, or do Amazon payouts have the same issue?
Amazon is a bit better, but same story.
